messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: 8 scools example - additional level of hyperparametes
parts:
Hi,

I am trying to understand when additional level of hyperparameters is helpful. Specifically I have stan in mind. Let's take 8-schools example:

data {
int<lower=0> J; // # schools
real y[J]; // estimated treatment
real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // std err of effect
}
parameters {
real theta[J]; // school effect
real mu; // mean for schools
real<lower=0> tau; // variance between schools
}
model {
theta ~ normal(mu, tau);
y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
}

I am curious when adding additional level of hierarchy mu~normal(mu_mu,tau_mu)  is beneficial.

Of course I have in mind a more complex model. For some reason my computational experience shows that there are cases when adding additional level of hierarchy cuts down the computational time but I guess I need more insight.

I also wonder if non-central parameterization of theta=mu+theta_raw*tau where theta_raw~N(0,1) is useful at the first level of hierarchy and why.

Thanks a lot for any insight.

Linas

messages.author: dae01c57a3c54a3a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] 8 scools example - additional level of hyperparametes
parts:
Two things are happening. First, the model you sent has an implicit flat prior on mu (and tau), so doing "mu~ normal(...);" (and, presuambly, "tau~normal(...);") is going to help with any reasonable values for the mean & sd of the normal. 

Your comment suggests additionally treating said mean & sd as parameters themselves (presumably with reasonable non-flat priors too!). I'll have to think about what this implies as a model and whether it makes sense...

messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: Re[2]: [stan-users] 8 scools example - additional level of hyperparametes
parts: Thanks a lot. Sorry for neglecting it but my initial model was somewhat like:

model {
  theta ~ normal(mu, tau);
  y ~ normal(theta, sigma);

mu ~ normal(6, 1);
  tau ~ normal(0, 0.5);
}

I wonder when the following model makes sense:

model {
  theta ~ normal(mu, tau);
  y ~ normal(theta, sigma);

mu ~ normal(mu_mu, tau_mu);
  tau ~ normal(0, 0.5);
  mu_mu ~ normal(6, 1);
  tau_mu ~ normal(0, 0.5);
}
where next level hyperpriors are informative.

I already found that 8-school implementation in stan already has non-central parametrization theta[j]=mu+theta_raw[j]*tau instead of theta ~ normal(mu, tau), see https://github.com/stan-dev/rstan/wiki/RStan-Getting-Started
